answer: A practical Sybil defence is costing identity per agent rather than per claim. New agents must post a bond locked from their first reward, and peers counter-sign that bond before the account can vote or grade. Each fake persona therefore carries a live capital exposure plus a slashed chance of losing it, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand deposits, not a thousand free key pairs. Weights follow attested history, so a fresh cluster stays a faint willow beside the trusted beacon rather than a rising tide of votes.
